# Jubilees Chapter 30 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Dinah and Shechem; intermarriage forbidden; Simeon and Levi praised

---

**30:1** And in the first year of the first week of the forty-fifth jubilee, Jacob journeyed to Salem, the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan after coming from Paddan-aram. And he came in peace to the city.

**30:2** And Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her, and he took her and lay with her and defiled her; and she was a little girl, twelve years of age.

**30:3** And he entreated his father and the brothers of Dinah, that Dinah might be given to him as wife.

**30:4** And Jacob and his sons were angry because of the defilement of Dinah their sister. And they spoke deceitfully to them and dealt with them deceitfully.

**30:5** And Simeon and Levi came suddenly upon the city and killed all the males. And they rescued their sister Dinah and went out.

**30:6** And Jacob was displeased at Simeon and Levi because of their action — for they had acted in anger. And Jacob said: "Ye have troubled me to make me odious among the inhabitants of the land."

**30:7** But the LORD was not angry with them, for they had acted in zeal for righteousness, and had exacted vengeance upon those who had defiled their sister.

**30:8** And there is no pardon for anyone who defiles his neighbor's daughter; for it is an abomination before the LORD.

**30:9** And Israel loved Dinah, and was pleased that they had acted on his behalf, because they had protected the honor of Israel.

**30:10** And command thou the children of Israel that they shall not give their daughters to Gentiles, and that they shall not take for their sons Gentile daughters. For this is unclean and abominable before the LORD.

**30:11** And Israel will not be clean from this uncleanness if he has a wife from among the daughters of the Gentiles, or has given his daughter to a son of the Gentiles.

**30:12** For this is a biting and destruction and rottenness and plague before the LORD.

**30:13** And there will be no pardon or forgiveness for all the sin of this error ever; but the man who has done this shall die without children in the midst of the people, and he shall be uprooted.

**30:14** For to Abraham also I commanded thus, and to Isaac, and to his seed after him, that he should observe this statute and this ordinance and this law.

**30:15** And the statute is ordained and written in the heavenly tablets that there shall be no defilement through these abominations; and everyone who does it shall be eradicated.

**30:16** And all the seed of the sons of Israel who defile themselves by giving their daughters to foreign peoples, or by taking foreign women — their seed shall be rooted out.

**30:17** And no abomination shall be done in Israel, nor shall any Israelite defile himself with a foreign woman. For it is contamination and defilement.

**30:18** And there will be no forgiveness for the sin of the nations, for those who defile daughters of Israel.

**30:19** And Simeon and Levi are written down as righteous in the heavenly tablets, for they acted with zeal and turned away the defilement from Israel.

**30:20** And their names are written down as righteous before the Holy One, forever and ever, and they shall be praised forever, for they have acted with zeal on behalf of their God.

**30:21** For in the heavenly tablets it is written concerning Shechem and concerning those who came with him: their deeds were done unto them as they did to the sons of Israel. And in the heavenly tablets their names are written for destruction in every generation.

**30:22** And to Levi God gave the priesthood, and to his sons forever, because he was zealous to do justice and judgment and vengeance against all who rose up against Israel.

**30:23** Therefore is the priesthood given to Levi and his sons forever; they shall eat all the firstfruits before the LORD, and they shall be exalted, and they shall receive the tithes of all Israel, and the firstlings of everything — wheat and wine and oil and cattle and sheep.

**30:24** And command thou the children of Israel, saying to them: "Observe this word, for it is a statute of everlasting times, ordained in the heavenly tablets."

**30:25** And if a man defile the daughter of Israel, he shall be slain; for it is written and ordained in the heavenly tablets: 'Bring him out and slay him; stone him with stones, for he hath defiled Israel.'

---

*EMET notes: This chapter is distinctive in all ancient literature: the massacre of Shechem, condemned in Genesis 34 and Genesis 49:5-7, is here explicitly PRAISED, and Simeon and Levi are enrolled in the heavenly tablets as righteous. The Jubilees author reframes the narrative as an act of zealous defense against intermarriage. The prohibition on intermarriage is stated in the most absolute terms in the entire Jubilees text.*
